text: The step builds against the plan's H row and declares the six rows the build also needs — the P5 agreement, the P6 notices, the P1 addressee, the P3 case state read and move answer, and the P7 package — as consumed contract rows with their placeholders rather than adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without those six rows and five of the operations have no published name.
read: The six rows are named in 12.2, faked in 12.8 and marked class C in the text; DP-05 is the one pattern row of the customer fact; the document run is recorded as a Temporal dependency on the P5 queue.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-decision
impact: The story can start on Day 1; the dependency map under-reports six rows until it is corrected

text: R-DS-23 is owned as the award effect only: the agreement, the notices, the record, the two lot columns and the case move belong to this story, while the price test R-DS-19, API-S6-003, the buyer columns and the LotAwarded event stay with RWB-S6-E6005-APP.
why: R-DS-23 names both the award and the documents in one sentence, the split plan gives its criterion to this key while the legacy endpoint row and the award operation belong to the award story, and the sibling stories attribute LotAwarded to that story.
read: The legacy AC2 words are kept unchanged, 12.1 and 12.3 are None with the sibling named, the A right is recorded as the award operation's, and section 18 names the split.
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of RWB-S6-E6005-APP
impact: No operation and no event are built here, and the award act and its event are proved where the award story is tested

text: The agreement and notice references are held in the decision record and in the custody of their owners, the lot status is written to AWARDED by this step, and REQ-S6-006 is traced as the nearest requirement of the slice.
why: debt_sale_lot has no column for the references, no source states that the award changes the lot status, and no FSD requirement or TSD traceability row names the agreement or the notices.
read: Section 11 records the references as the record's and the owners', section 9 declares the AWARDED write with the gap, and section 18 traces REQ-S6-006 with the note.
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward
impact: No column is added and no migration is created; a reference column and a requirement row can follow in a later change

text: The addressee of a notice is read on the rwb-source-data contract, travels inside the notice request only, and is kept in no column, record, log or event of this service; the notice types and the templates are versioned reference data of rwb-comms, rwb-document and rwb-decision with their values recorded as the placeholder.
why: The legacy step reads v_ace_customer, only rwb-source-data may read a v_ace_* view in the target, a notice needs its addressee, and no source gives the notice types, the templates or the masking rule of a sale letter.
read: DP-05 is the pattern row, 12.2 names the row with its placeholder, 12.8 fixes a fake that never answers an unmasked identifier, section 11 forbids the value in the schema and BR4 and BR10 forbid it in the record, the log and the workflow input.
confirm: Solution architect, the data steward and the owners of rwb-source-data and rwb-comms
impact: No personal data is held in this service; the notice types and templates are confirmed by their owners before the baseline is tagged

text: WIN is reached through rwb-comms for the despatch and through rwb-integration for the INT-14 letters file, and FEAT-OCC-07 is read as the P5 document generation with the P6 templates, so this story keeps its X and I rows at None and builds no file.
why: The FSD names WIN and FEAT-OCC-07 as the integration point and the prerequisite of the feature, and in the target both sit outside this service and outside the plan's C and X rows.
read: Section 12.9 records one outbound file that is not built here, 12.2 consumes the P6 notice issue which carries the despatch, and section 19 puts the WIN despatch and the INT-14 file with rwb-comms and rwb-integration.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-comms and rwb-integration
impact: No file and no external call is built here; the notice channel's rows are recorded for the dependency map

text: The story keeps wave 4 with release 30 April 2027 as the plan and the legacy epic give them, inside a service created in wave 3.
why: R5.6 gives EP06 the W-MAP wave 4 and raises one conflict per service and business epic, and the date is copied unchanged and tentative by rule.
read: The metadata carries wave 4 and the date with the tentative mark, section 2 states the two-wave delivery, and section 3 keeps the Day-1 start against the CON baseline.
impact: The build starts on Day 1 in the wave 3 service and the release stays as the plan states it

text: FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 are read from their module folders and stand in for the absent flat S6 extract; the R7.3 fill order is applied unchanged.
why: The run folder carries the S6 pair one level down and no flat S6 extract at the top of the extract folder, and the module files sit above any summary in the precedence order.
read: Every FSD and TSD value of sections 2 to 18 is taken from the two module files, the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, the legacy story and the Feature List rows of FEAT-OCC, and section 18 names the source text.
impact: No value is taken from a summary or a deck; the extract set is corrected in a later pass

why: Cited by _work/msr/editlog/B2-S6-009.md; see the story body for the default used.
